properties.description:
Every served tool's description states the job the way somebody states it when they want it done — not the way the tool is named — and a committed corpus of one query per tool is the standing check that the sentence was written from the job rather than tuned to the test.

DELIVERED 2026-09-11 (PR #476, merged): 68 sentences written from purpose, 8 descriptions trimmed to budget, corpus committed as crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/fixtures/find_tools_corpus.json with an acceptance test. Measured on main: 177 of 180 tools in find_tools' default top 5, up from a 114 baseline where 53 tools did not appear in the top 10 at all. Three tools sit at rank 6 and are exempt WITH THE MEASURED REASON, each beaten by short descriptions sharing incidental words. A second test walks the served surface and refuses any tool absent from the corpus, so a 181st tool cannot ship unfindable by omission.

THE HONESTY CHECK, AND WHY IT IS NOT A GATE: a sentence that merely copies its corpus query passes the committed test and still fails a user who words it differently. The guard is a held-out paraphrase corpus written from a different angle and never consulted while the sentences were written — 36 of 42, up from 16 after the rewrite it forced. It is deliberately NOT wired into CI, because folding it in would make it the next thing people tune to.

TWO SCORER REFINEMENTS WERE TRIED AND REVERTED on measurement — a 4-character floor on the name-prefix rule (neutral) and a gentler length normalisation (worse) — because a change the corpus does not reward is noise.
properties.name: Every served tool carries the job in a user's own words, and a committed 180-query corpus is the acceptance test that it was carried honestly
